claim_text: A leaker called Cyberleek says it posted a near-complete Xbox build of GTA 6 on Nov 19
summary: A leaker using the Cyberleek alias announced on Nov 19 that it was sharing a full November 2026 Xbox build of GTA 6, minus the main executable. Reports put it at about 209 GB.
detail: These outlets report the leaker's own posts, so they count as one source. Kotaku said it could not verify the files. The 209 GB figure comes from posts on social media relayed by the outlets; PC Gamer says about 200 GB from comments on a removed forum post.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Three outlets quote the leaker's announcement; none of them checked the files themselves.
notes: Leaker's own claim, relayed by the press.

claim_text: A security research group says the files look genuine
summary: TweakTown, relayed by TechRadar, says a security research group that tracks leaks examined the files and found real game assets, which led it to believe the leak is genuine.
detail: This is one assessment relayed by two outlets. PC Gamer and Kotaku said on Nov 19 they could not confirm the build was real, and TweakTown notes the dump is missing some system files. Rockstar and Take-Two have not said whether the files are real.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: One outside group says the assets look real; the company has not confirmed it.
notes: Outside assessment, counted as one source; TechRadar leans on it.

claim_text: Outlets report the leaker posted the main executable on Nov 23, ahead of its countdown
summary: GameGPU, Wccftech and DSOGaming report that on Nov 23 the leaker posted the missing Xbox executable. GameGPU adds that it is for build 1.0.2.1, came with checksums and is meant for emulation and PC recompilation projects.
detail: All three outlets relay the leaker's own posts, so they count as one source. None says it checked the file. DSOGaming stresses the file cannot be used to play the game on a PC. We have not seen the post and did not look at any download site.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Three outlets now report the drop, relaying the leaker's posts; none checked the file itself.
notes: Moved from Unverified on Nov 23: a second and third outlet reported the drop. Still the leaker's claim.

claim_text: The leaker tied the release to its memecoin
summary: The leaker said it would release the executable early if its memecoin hit a set market cap ($15 million, which GameGPU says was later lowered to $6 million), and in any case on Nov 23. GameSpot calls it a crypto grift.
detail: The terms are the leaker's own, relayed by outlets. GameSpot's pump-and-dump line is attributed to earlier reports and is not something we checked. Outlets report the executable came out on Nov 23 without the threshold being reached.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Several outlets quote the leaker's stated terms.
notes: Leaker's own terms, relayed. Counted as one source.

claim_text: Fake download sites may be spreading malware
summary: TechRadar says fake files posing as the game already circulate, made by scammers unrelated to the leaker. GameGPU and GameSpot also warn that copies may carry malware.
detail: These are warnings from outlets. We did not open any site or file and did not test anything. We name no site.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Three outlets warn of fake copies; none shows a specific sample.
notes: Do not download any copy; that is the outlets' advice too.

claim_text: How the leaker got the build
summary: No one has said how the build was obtained. TechRadar says a security research group guessed a Rockstar employee was compromised. That is one theory.
detail: TechRadar attributes the theory to TweakTown. The TweakTown article we read does not contain it, so we could not trace it. No company or law enforcement statement was found.
label: Unverified
why_it_supports: One outlet repeats a theory; nothing confirms it.

claim_text: Whether Rockstar or Take-Two confirmed the build is real or that they were breached
summary: Neither Rockstar nor Take-Two has publicly commented on the Nov 19 build or the executable that we could find. Rockstar has not said its systems were breached.
detail: GameGPU says Rockstar has not commented on the files' authenticity. We found no statement in newsroom or press coverage.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: The sources say there is no statement; we found none.

claim_text: Rockstar acknowledged earlier leaked gameplay videos in August
summary: In an Aug 26 public letter Rockstar called the leak of GTA 6 gameplay videos 'heartbreaking for our team'. The letter is about the August clips, not the November build, and does not say how they leaked.
detail: Game Informer and The Verge both print the letter in full, so they count as one source. Engadget reads it as the first public acknowledgement that the clips were real.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Two outlets print the company's own letter in full.
notes: Company statement relayed by outlets; August clips only.

claim_text: A court ordered subpoenas issued to Microsoft and Discord at Take-Two's request in August
summary: Take-Two asked a New York federal court on Aug 20, 2026 for DMCA subpoenas to Microsoft and Discord. Signed orders dated Aug 21 direct the clerk to issue both; a further order dated Aug 31 grants another subpoena to Discord.
detail: The filings and orders are from August, before the November build, and concern earlier leaks. They show the court directed the clerk to issue the subpoenas; they do not show what Microsoft or Discord handed over, and we found no later docket entry. The accounts and pages named in them are left out here. The Microsoft request is about its code-hosting service, not Xbox.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The requests and the signed orders, on the court docket, show the subpoenas were ordered issued.
notes: Court filings and orders, Tier 1. GameSpot repeats it. Updated Nov 23 with the orders.
